trends.name: Iran-US Military Escalation & Strait Disruption
trends.summary: Iran launched 8 ballistic missiles, 4 cruise missiles, and 36 UAVs at UAE on March 31, with Strait of Hormuz transit at historic lows (80% only Iranian/friendly vessels in March). EU allies (Italy, France, Spain) now denying US military aircraft landing permissions, signaling geopolitical fracture. Critical for energy prices, shipping costs, and inflation expectations.

trends.name: Eurozone Inflation Surging on Energy Crisis
trends.summary: Eurozone inflation jumped this month driven by surging energy prices tied to the Iran conflict. Further escalation could trigger additional price shocks. Market implications include ECB policy divergence and EUR weakness amid geopolitical uncertainty.

trends.name: Nvidia & AI Chipmaker Consolidation Play
trends.summary: Nvidia takes $2 billion stake in Marvell, driving 7% stock pop and signaling continued AI semiconductor consolidation. Signals shifting competitive dynamics in AI infrastructure as demand for data center hardware intensifies amid AI capex race.

trends.name: AI-Driven Data Center & Infrastructure Boom
trends.summary: Multiple converging signals: Bitdeer repositioning for AI data center wave, CoreWeave financing deal excitement, Oracle ramping AI spending despite layoffs, and AI agents rollout (Public platform). Reflects sustained investor appetite for AI infrastructure despite economic uncertainty.

trends.name: Software & Cloud Sector Divergence & Weakness
trends.summary: ServiceNow stock posting worst quarter on record while Snowflake leadership surprise triggers sell-off. SoftwareOne and other enterprise software firms face headwinds, suggesting investor rotation away from cloud/SaaS despite AI narrative. Key indicator of market risk appetite shift.

trends.name: Biotech & Pharma M&A Wave: Lilly's Mega Deals
trends.summary: Eli Lilly acquiring Centessa for up to $7.8 billion to secure sleep disorder/narcolepsy drug pipeline, leveraging Zepbound's expanded approval for sleep apnea. Signals aggressive pharma consolidation and GLP-1 derivative market expansion; biotech ETF ($XBI) posts best day since April 9.

trends.name: Energy Sector Leadership & Oil Price Dynamics
trends.summary: $XLE (energy ETF) best sector performer this month; outpacing industrials ($XLI). Iran conflict driving oil market premium, but $4/gallon gas unlikely to trigger Fed rate hikes—may support future cut potential. Key macro tailwind for energy equities.

trends.name: Macroeconomic Resilience vs. Market Correction Signals
trends.summary: Consumer confidence improved in March despite cost surges; job market viewed more positively. However, 20 stocks with double-digit March gains, retail investor pullback, and pension fund emergence suggest bifurcated market with defensive rotation. Dispersion favors systematic approaches.

trends.name: Industrial & Energy Infrastructure Capex Upturn
trends.summary: Quanta Services (PWR) Analyst/Investor Day and commentary on infrastructure investment outlook. Reflects broader capex cycle in utilities, grid upgrades, and energy transition. Tied to both geopolitical disruption needs and long-term infrastructure spending themes.

trends.name: Trump Geopolitical Isolation & NATO Tensions
trends.summary: Trump warns UK/France US won't provide military support; EU actively denying landing rights for Iran war operations. Warren Buffett's shift to Independent status reflects broader political/economic fracture. Markets pricing in geopolitical fragmentation and reduced US alliance credibility.

trends.name: Consumer & Specialty Retail Earnings Mixed Signals
trends.summary: Nike earnings report awaited amid cautious sentiment; Purple Innovation, Celsius earnings transcripts reviewed for competitive positioning. Beverage/discretionary spending under pressure but Celsius maintains non-competitive threat narrative. Consumer spending divergence widening.

trends.name: Oracle & Tech Layoffs Amid AI Investment Shift
trends.summary: Oracle cutting thousands of jobs while ramping AI spending—classic tech capex reallocation pattern. Reflects broad industry shift toward AI infrastructure and away from traditional software headcount. Signals continued margin pressure on legacy tech ops.
